extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs (ACs) for the AISTATS 2024 conference
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Area Chairs overseeing the AISTATS review process: assignment and oversight of reviewers, handling author feedback, organizing discussions, writing meta-reviews, making acceptance recommendations, and ensuring procedural and ethical compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify desk-rejection cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify desk-rejection cases (e.g., papers with unacceptable formatting issues, dual submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly check submissions after receiving the initial assignment and identify desk-reject and/or conflict-of-interest cases if applicable. Examples of format violations and desk-reject triggers include unacceptable formatting issues and dual submissions. If in doubt, mark it as a violation for Program Chairs to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help reviewer assignments (recruit and adjust reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help reviewer assignments by recruiting expert reviewers and adjusting reviewer assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every submission in your batch is matched with 5 suitable reviewers whom you can trust on this submission, ideally with a diverse set of opinions. Invest time before the reviewing process starts to ensure expert reviewers are assigned; recruit additional experts where necessary. If submissions are far from your expertise, contact your Senior AC for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure submissions have high-quality reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the submissions have high-quality reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively check reviewer expertise and the quality of reviews. If reviews are low-quality or diverging, recruit emergency reviewers, ask reviewers to rewrite/resubmit their review if appropriate, or consider providing your own review in extreme cases. Investing effort in reviewer selection reduces borderline and mis-judged cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reviewer responsiveness and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the review process and ensure reviewers are responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send reminders to reviewers for submitting reviews on time. Recruit emergency reviewers if you lack enough high-quality reviews or have diverging opinions—do so about 1 week before the review release date. Maintain contact and follow-up to keep the process on schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require evidence in reviewer assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reviewers provide their comments with evidence (e.g., references supporting claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer selects a categorical answer (e.g., “combinatorial approach” for novelty), ensure the reviewer provides corresponding references or justification in the free-text portion. Prompt reviewers to back claims with citations or explicit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle author feedback correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle author feedback: check it adheres to the provided template and read confidential comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the submitted author feedback document adheres to the instructions of the provided template. Read confidential comments from both reviewers and authors. Check if the reproducibility checklist is submitted if applicable—note that checklist availability is not used in acceptance decisions, but remind authors to attach it in camera-ready if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize reviewer discussions after author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize reviewer discussions after author feedback and ensure reviewers address rebuttal content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewers have read the author feedback document and ask them to update their review with e.g., a new paragraph starting “Post author feedback comments”. Initiate and lead discussions: read reviews and author feedback, list pros and cons and the major disagreements in your discussion post, and explicitly ask reviewers with very high/low scores to explain their opinions. Read confidential messages and, if needed, contact corresponding reviewers to address authors’ concerns without revealing authors' confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision making and meta-review responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make acceptance/rejection recommendations based on reviews, author feedback, discussions, and your own understanding of the submission; write the meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write meta-reviews on time and base them on your reading of the paper, the reviews, the author feedback, and reviewer discussions. The meta-review needs to provide a convincing justification about your decision (especially for rejections). The meta-review should augment the reviews and explain how reviews, author response, and discussions were used to arrive at your recommendation. Do not dismiss or ignore a review or author feedback unless you have a good reason, and if so explain this in your meta-review. For papers where reviewers cannot reach consensus, read the paper carefully, write a detailed meta-review, and discuss such cases with your SAC. For rejection decisions, provide comments about potential ways to improve the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on what to include and how to judge material when writing the meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t focus too much on scores; look carefully at comments. Judge the quality of the review rather than taking note of the reviewer’s confidence score. Compare reviewers’ answers regarding provided keywords and expertise, and compare with authors’ keywords to detect misunderstandings. Indicate you have read the author feedback and explicitly state whether the rebuttal addressed reviewers’ concerns. If you use information not in the reviews (e.g., new arguments from reviewer-AC discussions), tell the authors that you have done so and what that information is. If you overrule a unanimous reviewer opinion, the standards for your summary should be at the level of a full review; consider soliciting an auxiliary review. Attempt to take a decisive stand on borderline papers. Try to counter perceived biases—treat unfashionable subjects fairly and recognize risk-taking work may not yet be SOTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend oral presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend accepted submissions for oral talks where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on reviews, discussions, and your reading of the paper, recommend accepted submissions worthy of oral presentations. Provide justification for oral recommendation in the meta-review or relevant discussion fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve review-process issues and escalate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve any issue during the review process, e.g., by recruiting emergency reviewers, addressing concerns from both reviewers and authors, and/or raising concerns with Senior ACs and Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you encounter conflicts, suspected misconduct, or unresolvable review disagreements, take corrective steps (recruit reviewers, request clarifications) and escalate to SACs or Program Chairs when needed. Notify SAC/Program Chairs if you notice unethical or suspicious behavior involving authors or reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMT registration and profile maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Register on CMT and keep your profile up-to-date (conflicts, expertise topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure your profile on CMT is up-to-date: add conflicts of interest and select expertise topics. Import papers to your CMT account to facilitate bidding and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper bidding and initial assignment checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in bidding and check initial assignments for desk-reject and conflict-of-interest cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will assign papers using bids and matching algorithms (TPMS). After receiving initial assignment, quickly check for desk-rejects or COIs. Be flexible with papers outside your immediate expertise and contact Senior AC if you need help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer diversity of opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a diverse set of reviewer opinions for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers with varied perspectives to reduce groupthink and help resolve borderline cases. Diversity of opinion helps produce rigorous discussions and balanced meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit emergency reviewers when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit emergency reviewers if there are insufficient high-quality reviews or highly divergent reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check and solicit emergency reviews between Fri, Nov 17 2023 - Thur, Nov 23 2023 (example window). If one week before the review-release date you lack adequate reviews or reviews conflict substantially, recruit emergency experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and enforce format compliance and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforce page limit and other format rules during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During review, the main part of the submission should be 8 pages long; after that only references are allowed. Other format violations include anything that breaks anonymity, violates dual submission policy, changes format (margins or vertical spaces), or submitting main paper and appendix in the same PDF. If in doubt, mark it as a violation for Program Chairs to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the reproduction checklist is submitted if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that the availability of the reproducibility checklist is not used in acceptance decisions. However, remind authors to attach the reproduction checklist in camera-ready if applicable. Check for checklist submission during author feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and non-use of submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain strict confidentiality: do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions until they are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) to anyone without prior approval from Program Chairs. Code submitted for review cannot be distributed. Do not talk to other ACs/SACs about submissions assigned to you unless you have a justified reason and have consulted your SAC or Program Chairs first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback for rejected papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions with rejection decisions, provide comments regarding potential ways to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending rejection, include constructive suggestions authors can use to improve the work. This helps authors understand the decision and makes the process more useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt best practices: respect deadlines, respond promptly, be professional and empathetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect deadlines and respond to emails promptly. It is okay to be unavailable for short periods—notify your SAC if you will be unavailable for longer or during critical windows. Be professional, listen to reviewers and authors, and be familiar with submissions in your batch so you can justify your meta-review with technical arguments. Show empathy for reviewers' personal situations when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation and consultation when uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: When uncertain about decisions, reach out to your SAC as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers cannot reach consensus or you are unsure, consult your SAC. For cases where you may overrule reviewers or when reviews disagree strongly, discuss with SAC and consider soliciting auxiliary reviews.
